title: Sheaf scalar-Hom evaluation chain map and input naturality
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafification of sectionwise scalar extension and $U$ restriction of scalars, both applied termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $T(A)=S\otimes_R A$ for the underlying $R$-linear sheaf tensor, termwise. Write $H_R(P,J)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ and $H_S(K,N)=\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(K,N)$ for the actual product Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]; their local degree-$n$ sections have coordinates $f^i:P^i|_W\to J^{i+n}|_W$ on $\mathcal C/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. All pure tensors below mean their images under the tensor sheafification units [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and evaluation means the actual product projection followed by evaluation at the identity object of the slice.
For arbitrary $R$-complexes $P,J$, $S$-complex $N$, and $S$-linear chain map $q:EJ\to N$, there are an $R$-linear chain map
$$\alpha_{P,J}:T H_R(P,J)\longrightarrow H_R(P,TJ)$$
and a unique $S$-linear chain map
$$\sigma_{P,J,q}:E H_R(P,J)\longrightarrow H_S(EP,N)$$
with the following formulas over every slice, in every degree $n$ and coordinate $i$:
$$\alpha(s\otimes f)^i(p)=s\otimes f^i(p),\qquad \sigma_q(s\otimes f)^i(t\otimes p)=st\,q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p)).$$
Both commute with slice restriction and the signed Hom differentials. For chain maps $u:P'\to P$, $v:J\to J'$, $w:N\to N'$ and $q':EJ'\to N'$ with $q'\circ Ev=w\circ q$, their input naturality equations are
$$H_R(u,Tv)\circ\alpha_{P,J}=\alpha_{P',J'}\circ T H_R(u,v),$$
$$H_S(Eu,w)\circ\sigma_{P,J,q}=\sigma_{P',J',q'}\circ E H_R(u,v).$$
The notation $H(u,v)$ means precomposition with $u$ and postcomposition with $v$ in each coordinate. No flatness, boundedness, projectivity or K-injectivity is assumed; neither comparison is asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized ordinary adjunction D and chain isomorphisms nu and theta from lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction. The site fits inside the module universe, so the standard coefficient-universe sheafification instances supply the same hypotheses on every slice. Apply D.adjunction.homEquiv in every degree to obtain mutually inverse bijections between chain maps EA to N and A to UN. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction transports the chain equations and proves naturality of these bijections.

For q:EA to N, transpose q to h:A to UN. Define sigma as the inverse ordinary chain adjunction applied to H_R(id_P,h) followed by theta inverse. The inverse ordinary formula sends s tensor f to s times this family; theta inverse evaluates on t tensor x as t times h(f(x)). Thus the result is st q(1 tensor f(x)). All maps are already chain maps.

To prove uniqueness, apply the injective ordinary chain adjunction and postcompose with the invertible theta. Evaluate in every product coordinate and at every local x. The forward ordinary and theta formulas reduce this to the sigma formula with both scalars equal to 1. Equality of local evaluations gives equality on each slice by naturality, then equality of product-Hom maps by the limiting product projections. Naturality of sigma follows by the chain adjunction naturality, theta naturality, bifunctor composition, and the equality Eb followed by q prime equals q followed by w.

Define alpha as nu on H_R(P,A), followed by U sigma for q the identity of EA, theta, and H_R(id_P,nu_A inverse). The normalized nu and theta formulas and the sigma formula give its required local evaluation: nu_A inverse sends s times (1 tensor f(x)) to s tensor f(x). The identity s tensor x equals s times (1 tensor x) also follows by applying the inverse ordinary adjunction to its own image of the identity. Naturality follows from sigma naturality for q and q prime identities, theta naturality, and naturality of nu and its inverse. These constructions use arbitrary unbounded complexes and never apply extension to an infinite product.
